title: But he could no longer disbelieve in the reality of love, since God Himself had loved his individual soul with divine love from all eternity.
html_source:
A particular turning point for Stephen, who spent his younger years gradually pulling away from God.

Despite the dramatic turnaround, Joyce offers some explanation: Stephen now believes “since God Himself had loved his individual soul.”

And thus comes the irony of Stephen’s earlier education: The Jesuit school taught him not of holiness, but of reality—Stephen felt no love as Father Douglas pandied him.

anchor.text: But he could no longer disbelieve in the reality of love, since God Himself had loved his individual soul with divine love from all eternity.
anchor.prefix: iniquitous lust: it, too, had slipped beyond his grasp leaving his mind lucid and indifferent. This, it seemed, was the only love and that the only hate his soul would harbour.
